titles: Don't Kill the Spider in Your Corner. It Eats Bigger Spiders
Never Kill the Spider in Your Corner. It's Hunting Bigger Spiders
The Skinny Spider in Your Corner Is Hunting Something Bigger
pinned_comment: Shoe or spare? 👇 And if you have one in your corner, what's its name?

lines.say: That skinny spider in the corner of your ceiling is hunting something in your house.
lines.vis: FRAME 0: close on the cellar spider in her corner web, already moving (legs working silk). Night bedroom. Card: IT'S HUNTING

lines.say: Sometimes, something much bigger.
lines.vis: Cut to floor level: the shadow of a big hairy house spider crossing the floorboards.

lines.say: And you're standing on a chair, holding a shoe.
lines.vis: The viewer's shoe sole swings into the top of frame over the corner, casting a shadow on the web. The SQUISH / SPARE meter slides in at 30.

lines.say: Give me three questions before you swing.
lines.vis: Meatball hops between shoe and spider, arms out. Card: 3 QUESTIONS

lines.say: What is it hunting? Can it hurt you? And what happens if you leave it up there?
lines.vis: Three chips appear one per question: HUNTING? / HURT YOU? / LEAVE IT?

lines.say: This meter keeps score. If it says squish at the end, I'll hold the chair.
lines.vis: Meter pulses. Meatball steadies the chair, deadpan.

lines.say: Question one. What is it hunting?
lines.vis: Chapter card, 1.2 s max, over the corner web.

lines.say: Meet the cellar spider. Body about a quarter inch. Front legs about two inches.
lines.vis: Name card CELLAR SPIDER. Ruler gag: tiny body, absurdly long legs measured.

lines.say: Many cellar spiders have eight eyes, set in three little clusters.
lines.vis: Extreme close-up of the face: eyes in three groups blink out of sync.

lines.say: I call mine Carol.
lines.vis: A little name tag on the web: CAROL. Meatball waves; Carol waves one leg.

lines.say: Carol hangs upside down in a messy web and waits.
lines.vis: Carol upside down in the tangle, still.

lines.say: Flying insects. Woodlice. Anything that blunders in.
lines.vis: A fly, then a woodlouse, each snagged and wrapped in a beat.

lines.say: In one lab, cellar spiders were fed just one fly every three or four days, and still laid eggs.
lines.vis: Lab scene: a calendar flips 3-4 days, one fly delivered on a tiny plate.

lines.say: But flies are not why you should put the shoe down.
lines.vis: Back to the corner; shoe twitches.

lines.say: In England, someone emptied the cellar spider webs in one garden shed, over one summer, and counted the leftovers.
lines.vis: Shed interior, many corner webs. Meatball with tweezers and a tray.

lines.say: One hundred and two dead things.
lines.vis: Tally board fills: 102.

lines.say: Sixty-three of them were house spiders.
lines.vis: Card 63 OF 102, the board sorts into a big pile of house spiders.

lines.say: Six were other cellar spiders.
lines.vis: The six drop into a second pile labelled CELLAR SPIDERS. Carol looks away, whistling.

lines.say: The rest were spider bits too broken to name. Every single leftover was a spider.
lines.vis: Full circle chart, no slices of anything else: 63 HOUSE SPIDERS / 6 CELLAR SPIDERS / 33 UNIDENTIFIED SPIDER BITS.

lines.say: And she doesn't stop at her own size.
lines.vis: The big shadow from the cold open returns on the floor.

lines.say: She has been recorded eating giant house spiders. The big ones.
lines.vis: Reveal the giant house spider, huge next to Carol. Size-compare card.

lines.say: British spider experts say she may even be why the big ones are getting rarer in some places.
lines.vis: A row of big house spiders; one by one they become empty silhouettes with question marks.

lines.say: Picture it. Two in the morning. The big one comes down your wall, fast.
lines.vis: Dramatised hunt, night wall: the giant house spider descends toward the corner. Low camera, long shadow.

lines.say: Carol is a fraction of its size, hanging there like a loose thread.
lines.vis: Carol motionless, tiny in frame beside the approaching giant. (Size shown as 'much smaller', no number on screen.)

lines.say: It walks straight under her.
lines.vis: The giant passes beneath the web. Beat of silence, music drops out.

lines.say: So how does a quarter-inch spider with legs like thread beat something that size?
lines.vis: Versus card: CAROL vs THE BIG ONE. Pause-and-reveal 1 of 3.

lines.say: She keeps her distance. That's what the legs are for.
lines.vis: Carol keeps her body back; legs reach across the gap.

lines.say: She stays out of reach and flicks silk over it with her back legs.
lines.vis: Close on the two hind legs flicking silk strands over the big spider.

lines.say: Left, right, left, right. Like wrapping a burrito she's scared of.
lines.vis: Alternating flicks; the big spider becomes a silk bundle.

lines.say: Once it's tied up, she moves in and bites.
lines.vis: Carol steps in to the wrapped bundle.

lines.say: I watched her do it once. I did not sleep. But I respected it.
lines.vis: Meatball in bed, eyes wide open, slow nod.

lines.say: And she doesn't only hunt at home.
lines.vis: Carol leaves her corner, walking the ceiling.

lines.say: A cellar spider will walk into another spider's web. On purpose.
lines.vis: Carol steps onto a neat web that belongs to another spider.

lines.say: In there she eats the trapped insects, the eggs, and the spider who built it.
lines.vis: Three quick icons crossed off: insect, egg sac, owner.

lines.say: Scientists call it aggressive mimicry.
lines.vis: Card: AGGRESSIVE MIMICRY

lines.say: Some cellar spiders jiggle the web to lure the owner over. Then they eat the owner.
lines.vis: A leg plucks the web; the owner hurries over; cut to a wrapped bundle.

lines.say: It's ringing the doorbell and eating whoever answers.
lines.vis: Doorbell gag on the web.

lines.say: Now the question everyone asks. Does she eat brown recluses?
lines.vis: A brown recluse silhouette with a question mark.

lines.say: In a lab in Brazil, cellar spiders killed recluse spiders up to five times heavier than they were.
lines.vis: Lab arena: Carol vs a much heavier recluse (label: SOUTH AMERICAN RECLUSE). Scale with a 5x weight.

lines.say: That was a South American recluse, in a lab. And given a choice, they went for the insects instead.
lines.vis: Carol ignores the recluse and takes the fly. Recluse looks offended.

lines.say: In Kansas, researchers checked fifty houses.
lines.vis: Map pin on Kansas; a row of little houses, count 50.

lines.say: In about two out of three, they found house spiders, cellar spiders included, preying on recluses, or the evidence of it.
lines.vis: Two thirds of the houses light up.

lines.say: But the same study said don't count on it. As pest control, it's limited.
lines.vis: Stamp over the houses: NOT A CURE.

lines.say: Carol is not a recluse cure. At best, a bonus.
lines.vis: Carol shrugs with four legs.

lines.say: Question one, answered. She hunts other spiders, even big ones.
lines.vis: Chip 1 gets a tick. Meter settles.

lines.say: But you've heard the other thing about her.
lines.vis: The shoe drifts lower. Whisper lines around Carol.

lines.say: Question two. Can it hurt you?
lines.vis: Chapter card, 1.2 s max.

lines.say: Here's the rumor. Daddy longlegs have the deadliest venom of any spider, but their fangs are too small to bite you.
lines.vis: Card THE RUMOR; a skull-and-crossbones thought bubble over Carol.

lines.say: If that's true, I'll hand you the other shoe.
lines.vis: Meatball offers a second shoe. Meter drops hard.

lines.say: Problem one. Three different animals get called daddy longlegs.
lines.vis: Police-lineup wall, three figures in shadow.

lines.say: The harvestman. One round body, two eyes. Not a spider. No fangs, no venom.
lines.vis: Light on suspect 1: harvestman. Label: NOT A SPIDER.

lines.say: The crane fly. Six legs and wings. It's an insect.
lines.vis: Light on suspect 2: crane fly. Label: INSECT.

lines.say: And Carol. Two body parts, eight legs, and a web in your corner. The only real spider of the three.
lines.vis: Light on suspect 3: Carol. Label: THE SPIDER.

lines.say: So the rumor can't even agree on which animal it means.
lines.vis: All three point at each other.

lines.say: Tell me in the comments which of the three you've been calling daddy longlegs.
lines.vis: The three suspects hold up numbers 1, 2, 3. Small comment-bubble icon.

lines.say: Problem two. There was never any science behind it. The Burke Museum's spider expert calls it an urban legend.
lines.vis: Card URBAN LEGEND stamped across THE RUMOR.

lines.say: She does have venom. Almost every spider does. The same expert says there's nothing special about hers.
lines.vis: Carol with a tiny labelled venom bottle: REGULAR.

lines.say: So where did the rumor start? The Australian Museum has a guess.
lines.vis: Globe spins to Australia.

lines.say: People saw her kill redbacks, Australia's cousin of the black widow, and figured her venom must be worse.
lines.vis: Carol over a wrapped redback; onlookers gasp and jump to the wrong conclusion (thought bubble: SUPER VENOM?).

lines.say: It isn't. She just wraps first and bites later.
lines.vis: Replay of the silk flick, small.

lines.say: Then in 2019, scientists finally tested the venom of one kind of cellar spider.
lines.vis: Lab scene, card 2019.

lines.say: On crickets, it worked. Paralysis.
lines.vis: A cricket freezes mid-hop.

lines.say: On us? They concluded the venom of one spider is not deadly to humans or other mammals.
lines.vis: Card NOT DEADLY TO HUMANS.

lines.say: And they traced the scary reputation to rumor and anecdote.
lines.vis: The skull thought bubble pops.

lines.say: What about the fangs? That paper says this spider's fangs can get through soft human skin.
lines.vis: Close-up diagram: tiny fangs, skin line. Honest beat: meter dips 2.

lines.say: A TV show tried it for real. A cellar spider bit a person on camera.
lines.vis: Meatball's arm in a clear box with one spider, TV camera icon. No real footage, no show logo.

lines.say: The result was a mild sting that faded fast.
lines.vis: Meatball: tiny 'ow', then shrug.

lines.say: The worst bite in that paper left a sore about one millimeter wide.
lines.vis: A ruler against Meatball's knuckle: a dot, labelled 1 MM. Meter dips a little.

lines.say: So the rumor fails at both ends. No deadly venom. And at least one kind can bite.
lines.vis: Both halves of THE RUMOR card crack and fall.

lines.say: Penn State says cellar spiders aren't known to bite people.
lines.vis: Source chip: PENN STATE EXTENSION.

lines.say: And a spider expert at U.C. Riverside knows of no published case of its venom poisoning a person.
lines.vis: Source chip: UC RIVERSIDE.

lines.say: So can it hurt you? Barely. Recorded bites were mild.
lines.vis: Chip 2 gets a tick.

lines.say: My roommate still sleeps with the light on. That's between them and the electric bill.
lines.vis: Roommate lump under blanket, lamp blazing, meter of an electric bill spinning.

lines.say: Meter check. Carol is winning.
lines.vis: Meter fills the frame for a beat at 76.

lines.say: But I promised a fair fight. Here is the case for the shoe. And it's a good one.
lines.vis: The shoe gets a spotlight and a little lawyer's tie.

lines.say: Question three. What happens if you leave her up there?
lines.vis: Chapter card, 1.2 s max.

lines.say: More Carols.
lines.vis: A second, third, fourth name tag appear.

lines.say: She carries her eggs in her jaws. A little bundle, held in her mouth, while she hangs upside down.
lines.vis: Close on Carol holding the egg bundle in her jaws.

lines.say: A few dozen eggs in a bundle.
lines.vis: Card ABOUT 50 EGGS.

lines.say: When she's hungry, she parks the eggs in the web, eats, and picks them back up.
lines.vis: She hangs the bundle on a strand like a coat, eats, collects it.

lines.say: In a lab in Tokyo, females made between two and eight bundles each.
lines.vis: Lab shelf: bundles count 2... up to 8.

lines.say: Two to three weeks later, the eggs hatch.
lines.vis: Calendar pages; bundle bursts into specks.

lines.say: The babies stay on mom's web for a few days. Then they go and find corners of their own.
lines.vis: Tiny spiders fan out along the ceiling.

lines.say: Your corners.
lines.vis: Every corner of the room gains a tiny web.

lines.say: And growing up takes them months, up to about a year.
lines.vis: Growth chart on the wall, baby to adult.

lines.say: She isn't leaving soon either. In that lab, females lived about a year and a half as adults. The oldest passed two years.
lines.vis: Carol with a tiny birthday hat, then a second one.

lines.say: Then there's the mess.
lines.vis: Camera pulls back: dusty webs.

lines.say: Her web is not a neat wheel. It's a tangle.
lines.vis: Side by side: tidy orb web vs Carol's tangle.

lines.say: It builds up, and it collects dust.
lines.vis: Time lapse: web greys with dust.

lines.say: One web was reported covering a square meter of ceiling. That's a bath towel of cobweb.
lines.vis: A bath towel outline on the ceiling filled with web.

lines.say: And the family stays. In Finland, scientists report colonies in some buildings for more than ten years.
lines.vis: A building in snow; calendar spins ten years; windows full of little webs.

lines.say: So the shoe has a point. One Carol can become a ceiling of Carols.
lines.vis: Ceiling of name tags. The shoe looms lowest of the whole episode.

lines.say: Look at the meter. The shoe is back in front.
lines.vis: Meter in the red at 36, alarm blink.

lines.say: But read the charge sheet out loud.
lines.vis: Courtroom gag: a one-line charge sheet unrolls.

lines.say: The University of California says cellar spiders mostly cause trouble one way. Messy cobwebs.
lines.vis: Charge sheet text: 1. COBWEBS. Source chip UC IPM.

lines.say: That's the main charge.
lines.vis: The sheet has one big line and some very small print. Meatball squints at the small print, shrugs.

lines.say: Kentucky's entomologists call her harmless. Utah State lists her as beneficial.
lines.vis: Two source chips stamp: HARMLESS, BENEFICIAL.

lines.say: The crime is bad housekeeping. There's a tool for that, and we'll get to it.
lines.vis: A vacuum peeks in from the edge of frame, then hides.

lines.say: First, something the shoe doesn't know. Carol's corner is not a safe place.
lines.vis: Corner at night; another pair of eyes appears.

lines.say: When a jumping spider turns up, she does this.
lines.vis: A jumping spider stalks in. Pause-and-reveal 2 of 3.

lines.say: She whirls. Round and round in her web until she's a blur.
lines.vis: Carol gyrates in a circle, motion-blurred.

lines.say: You can see it yourself. Touch the web gently and she whirls into a blur.
lines.vis: Meatball's finger taps a strand; blur.

lines.say: In one lab study, jumping spiders set off the long whirls. Hunters from eight other spider families hardly ever did.
lines.vis: Eight different spider silhouettes pass: Carol gives each a quick short shimmy. The jumping spider appears: the long blur.

lines.say: The blur may make her hard for a jumping spider to lock onto.
lines.vis: The jumping spider's eyes spin; it gives up.

lines.say: And she doesn't always win.
lines.vis: Mood drop: darker corner.

lines.say: In a lab, scientists paired ten cellar spiders with ten noble false widows.
lines.vis: Ten small arenas, Carol vs false widow in each.

lines.say: Seven of the ten cellar spiders ended up dead, wrapped in false widow silk.
lines.vis: Seven arenas go grey; card 7 OF 10.

lines.say: In California, a different cellar spider, the marbled one, has pushed her kind out.
lines.vis: Map pin on California; a marbled cellar spider takes over a corner.

lines.say: So she's no monster. She's a quarter inch of spider in a rough neighborhood.
lines.vis: Carol small in a big dark room.

lines.say: And she's only in that neighborhood because of us.
lines.vis: Camera pulls out through the wall to the house exterior.

lines.say: In the wild, cellar spiders live in cave mouths and cracks in cliffs.
lines.vis: Cave mouth with tangle webs.

lines.say: Hers is a warm-climate species that people carried around the world.
lines.vis: Globe with little suitcases hopping continent to continent.

lines.say: In cold places she lives almost entirely inside our buildings. That's the cellar in cellar spider.
lines.vis: Snow outside, warm cellar inside, Carol by the boiler.

lines.say: In Britain she has been spreading north for decades. The likely reason is central heating.
lines.vis: Map of Britain; radiators light up northward.

lines.say: Your furnace is her climate.
lines.vis: Carol basking over a radiator like a beach.

lines.say: Which is why I don't put mine outside in January. Experts say she can't take real cold.
lines.vis: Meatball opens the door to a blizzard, looks at Carol, closes it.

lines.say: So here's the deal.
lines.vis: Meatball between shoe and spider again, holding up a contract.

lines.say: Keep the spider. Lose the cobwebs.
lines.vis: Card KEEP THE SPIDER / LOSE THE WEBS.
lines.card: KEEP THE SPIDER, LOSE THE WEBS

lines.say: A vacuum or a broom takes out old webs, and egg sacs too. That's from the University of Kentucky.
lines.vis: The vacuum finally enters; dusty webs vanish. Source chip.

lines.say: Want fewer Carols? Iowa State says vacuum every few weeks until new webs stop appearing.
lines.vis: Calendar: vacuum icon every few weeks; webs count down.

lines.say: Skip the spray. Iowa State says insecticides work poorly on her, and California says you generally don't need pesticides for spiders.
lines.vis: Spray can with a red X. Source chips.

lines.say: Seal the gaps around your windows and doors, and clear the clutter. Fewer bugs get in, and there are fewer places to hang a web.
lines.vis: Caulk gun along a window frame; boxes cleared from a corner.

lines.say: And if she's in a bad spot, like right over your pillow, put a jar over her, slide paper underneath, and carry her out.
lines.vis: Jar and card move, step by step.

lines.say: In winter, I carry mine to the basement.
lines.vis: Meatball tiptoes downstairs with the jar; Carol waves.

lines.say: Final score.
lines.vis: Meter centre frame. Pause-and-reveal 3 of 3.

lines.say: What is she hunting? Other spiders, even big ones.
lines.vis: Chip 1 replays: wrapped big spider.

lines.say: Can she hurt you? Barely. Recorded bites were mild.
lines.vis: Chip 2 replays: cracked rumor card.

lines.say: What if you leave her? You'll need a vacuum. And you'll have a bodyguard with a body the size of a grain of rice.
lines.vis: Chip 3: vacuum plus Carol in tiny sunglasses.

lines.say: Verdict. Put the shoe down.
lines.vis: Meter slams to SPARE. Stamp: SPARE. The shoe lifts out of frame.

lines.say: Oh, and that big one from the start? Here it comes.
lines.vis: The big house spider walks in under the corner.

lines.say: Carol's got it.
lines.vis: Two hind legs start flicking silk. Cut before the bite.

lines.say: Next time, the thirty-legged thing in your bathroom. It's hunting something too.
lines.vis: Silhouette of a house centipede on bathroom tile.

lines.say: Subscribe so you're here for it. Until then, here are eight more bugs. Three to keep. Five to kill.
lines.vis: END SCREEN: WATCH NEXT slot for Kill-or-Keep Part 2, subscribe slot. Hold 12 s under music.
